_comment: FieldKit relay egg for Pterodactyl. Import under Admin -> Nests -> Import Egg. The image fieldkit-relay:1 is built ON the Pterodactyl machine (docker build -t fieldkit-relay:1 deploy/bastion1); Wings cannot pull it from anywhere, falls back to the local image with that tag, and uses it. The relay's code and the tunnel programs are inside the image; the only file you upload is config.json. See relay/BROWSER.md.
name: FieldKit Relay
author: fieldkit@localhost
description: The FieldKit relay: encrypted vault storage, messaging, updates, the streamed browser, and RUNNER's ticket service. Code, Chromium, cloudflared and tailscale are all in the image; the server folder holds only config.json and the data the relay writes.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# The relay's code is inside the image now. This only makes the data
# folder and says which ONE file to upload.
mkdir -p /mnt/server/data
cat > /mnt/server/UPLOAD-THESE.txt <<'EOF'
Upload ONE file into /home/container:

  config.json      (from deploy/relay-upload/ on the dev PC)

That is all. The relay's code, Chromium, cloudflared and tailscale
are inside the image. Leave the Startup tab's Main File as
/opt/fieldkit/relay/start.js.

Do NOT upload release-key.json. It signs releases and belongs on the
development machine only.
EOF
echo 'FieldKit relay: directory ready. Upload config.json.'

variables.name: Main File
variables.description: The file the relay starts from. /opt/fieldkit/relay/start.js is the copy inside the image (brings up the tunnel, then the relay). start.js / server.js would be copies uploaded into the server folder, which is the old way.

variables.name: Config File
variables.description: Path to the relay's config.json. The default is the one you upload into the server folder.
